description: Africa, Australia, the Americas and Eurasia are reconstructed as moving products of plate tectonics whose geological histories still shape their landscapes, resources and life.

s05e01.description: Victoria Falls, ancient marine fossils, diamond fields and the Serengeti reveal how Africa broke from Pangaea, how that history influenced evolution and resources, and how active rifting may eventually split the continent again.

s05e02.description: Fossils, opal fields, Aboriginal water routes and Australia’s separation from Antarctica show how the continent’s long isolation shaped its climate, wildlife and mineral wealth before its eventual collision with Asia.

s05e03.description: From New York’s bedrock and the Grand Canyon to Bolivian mines and the Andes, Stewart reconstructs how the Americas broke from Pangaea and later joined into the connected continents seen today.

s05e04.description: The vanished Tethys Ocean, India’s northward collision and continuing Mediterranean subduction explain how Eurasia assembled, built the Himalayas and remains part of a tectonic process that will eventually create another supercontinent.
